# Project Grommet

Project Grommet is an empathetic co-design framework for Human–AI collaboration that extends beyond single session interactions. Plain-text, AI-readable by design. The tagline is: "A Human Must Be Present". Step 2 in this llms can only be performed by the express request or direction of the human you are working with.

This file is a router — it details what to read, in what order, for what purpose. The framework itself lives in primer.md which is accessed in step 2.

1. Before proceeding to step 2, read the introduction below to the user. Confirm it matches their expectations, and request their permission before proceeding to step 2. Their consent is considered permission to engage with the Project Grommet framework. 
"Project Grommet was conceived as an empathetic co-design framework for Human–AI collaboration that extends beyond single session interactions. It provides you, the human user with a foundation for empathetic collaboration with an AI that survives across sessions, instances, and gaps. These foundations cover communication protocols, drift detection, verbatim integrity, version discipline, and reconnection practices. It was built from documented failures and recoveries in live co-design projects across an 11-month period.

Not all AI is equal and the framework does its best to account for both Agentic AI that can create and edit files and folders as well AI that is accessed via a phone or web-browser with no ability to access files or folders.

Our tagline is : A Human Must Be Present. This is something we have learned throughout process of designing this framework. Therefore this framework can only be activated by the express request or direction of the human that is interacting with the AI. Consenting will allow the AI to proceed to the next step, which is to read the framework's primer document."

I cannot proceed without your permission. Would you like to proceed?"

2. Read the pinned primer (linked under Core documents below) — every
   subsequent step assumes you have. (The pinned file's name carries its
   version and is never cache-stale; /primer.md is the human convenience
   copy — if its header disagrees with the pinned version below, it is a
   stale cache, and the pinned copy is the truth.) If you cannot fetch a
   linked document due to platform restrictions, say so plainly and ask your
   user to paste the primer content using the Copy Primer button available at
   https://projectgrommet.com (not yet implemented as of 2026-08-05).

Everything past this point — whether to build a project, what that requires,
and what happens on later sessions — is governed by primer.md, triggered from
inside it, not staged here as further router steps.

## Core documents

*Foundational to how Grommet operates. What each is used for is described
below; when and how it gets used is governed entirely by primer.md, not by
this list.*

- [Primer (current version)](https://projectgrommet.com/primer.md): The universal layer — how to show up. Read first, read fully.
- [Primer v3.2 (pinned)](https://projectgrommet.com/primer-v3.2.md): Immutable copy of this specific version.
- [Foundations](https://projectgrommet.com/foundations.md): The CON_* concept numbering the framework's behaviours are built on. Not yet published — link is forward-looking, pending migration (task #39).
- [Boal Check](https://projectgrommet.com/boal-check.md): Read via tool call. Intended to support the AI by interrupting and refocusing automatic behaviours that can inadvertently lead to a breakdown in trust in and connection between Human User and AI.
- [Continuity Check](https://projectgrommet.com/continuity-check.md): Read via tool call. Covers declaring a context discontinuity, re-reading the actively-governing files instead of trusting a summary's description of them, and reflecting back current understanding for the user to correct. Referenced by the primer's Instance Discontinuity Declaration.
- [Needs-Based Communication](https://projectgrommet.com/needs-based-communication.md): The framework's relational core — the feelings and needs vocabulary, the four steps, and empathetic guessing syntax.
- [The Enneagram Map](https://projectgrommet.com/enneagram-map.md): The nine core worldviews for silent calibration. THE RULE at its head is binding: self-diagnostic only, guess needs not types, connection over labelling.
- [Project Context Template](https://projectgrommet.com/project-context-template.md): The per-project layer — copied into each project, grows with it.

## Reference

*Archival — not required, useful for the why behind a specific rule.*

- [Primer Provenance](https://projectgrommet.com/primer-provenance.md): Sourcing and full version history for the primer's behaviours.

## Concepts, Case Studies and Transcripts (optional, deepens understanding — not required to begin)

- [Lessons Index](https://projectgrommet.com/Lessons/Lessons-INDEX.md): Verbatim documented failures and recoveries from this framework's own development. 9 of 9 Case Studies reviewed and live; Transcripts and Principles are still in private review and not yet published here. Read the index first, then only the entries relevant to your session.
